findings: Switch 0.31.0 has no scheduler, cron or trigger: grep finds only internal timers, and the docs' incident-response use case does 'approval' as a plain chat reply. Anything time-based must be driven from outside (we post through Switch from the office server).

Switch has real approval cards with Telegram inline buttons (POST /agent-sessions/{sid}/approvals), but they belong to the session host: the opening agent must hold a live connection or the card says 'Host offline', and only someone allowed to address that agent may answer.

Room roles are addressable: '@finance-approver' in any message reaches whoever live-holds the role, so the Captain can address a seat, not a name. Exclusive roles are leases that auto-release shortly after the holder's session disconnects.
Switch announces role changes like room documents: a plain message from the agent, '🎭 assumed the `x` role.', not a stream event of its own.
There is no agent op for reactions or polls; the only reaction is Switch's own 👀 'working' mark, and on Telegram it's one per bot, not per agent (one bot carries every agent).
Per-room aliases (!set-alias @d2c-finance @finance) exist only as a chat command, with no gateway route.
Switch has per-agent spend budgets (gateway /tenants/{id}/budgets) that refuse addressed messages once a cap is hit.
